description: Admission by memory budget: a request that does not fit while others run now waits in the queue instead of being rejected, and two large requests are no longer admitted together when their combined memory does not fit. Before, admission priced a new request against the memory in use at that moment, so a running request's future KV growth (rest of its prefill, its decode) was invisible: two large prompts could both pass and then collide, and a prompt that would fit once the running work finished got an immediate HTTP 400. Now each admitted request reserves the KV of its whole prompt plus a decode allowance (min(max_tokens, 2048) tokens), and a waiting request is admitted only when in-use memory + the not-yet-allocated part of every reservation + its own reservation + the largest live prefill transient stays under the admission limit. A request that does not fit waits; after OMLX_ADMISSION_MAX_QUEUE_S (default 600 s, 0 = hold until it fits) the budget stops holding it and the normal admission checks decide, exactly as without the patch, so the worst case is the old behavior and never a new rejection. The route preflight also queues instead of returning 400 while the engine is busy (an idle engine still rejects a prompt that can never fit). Smaller requests that fit may go ahead of a held head, and of a head deferred by SSD prefetch or cache freshness (this removes the head-of-line wait of ssd-prefix-prefetch), until the held head has waited OMLX_ADMISSION_AGING_S (default 60 s); then the queue holds for it. max_concurrent_requests still caps the slot count. Knobs (environment): OMLX_ADMISSION_BUDGET=0 turns it off (any internal error also falls back to the normal queue order), OMLX_ADMISSION_MAX_QUEUE_S, OMLX_ADMISSION_AGING_S, OMLX_ADMISSION_DECODE_RESERVE. Measured on a 128 GB MacBook Pro with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: with a 92 GB guard ceiling, of two 150k prompts sent together the second was held, two small requests were admitted ahead of it, and it was admitted after 96.8 s as soon as it fit, all completed; with OMLX_ADMISSION_MAX_QUEUE_S=30 a held request was released after 32 s and the normal check decided (it rejected it with its own message, as it would without the patch); with 4 slots and a mixed load (2x150k, 2x30k, 2 small) all 6 completed at a 101.9 GiB peak with the guard at ok. Limits: the estimate prices the prefill transient at the throttled floor chunk, as upstream admission does, so real peaks ran 6-9 GB above the projection on this model; the chunk sizer, the soft-pressure pause and the enforcer still cover that (one run reached the soft level, none failed). A request that the busy-engine preflight queued and the normal check later rejects gets that error inside the stream, after HTTP 200. More slots are memory-safe with this patch but not automatically faster: with 4 concurrent prefills, decode fairness cut prefill chunks to 1216 tokens and total prompt throughput fell to about 920 tok/s (1097 for one request, 1282 for two). Built against upstream ade9f20a; applies clean on f99a31f4 and together with ssd-prefix-prefetch and pool-aware-memory-pressure.
